You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Cinder School microgrid","question":"Can the project report the backup trial as complete?","claims":{"A":"The battery supplied emergency loads continuously for 60 minutes on Thursday.","B":"The diesel generator was connected for the trial.","C":"The trial started on Thursday at 08:00."},"sources":{"S1":"generator log shows the diesel generator was disconnected for the trial.","S2":"trial sign-in records the start Thursday at 08:00.","S3":"mobile dashboard reports a battery runtime estimate of 62 minutes. An email calls the trial a success based on that estimate."},"follow_up":{"S4":"independent inline power logger records the battery supplying the emergency loads without interruption for the first 60 minutes Thursday."}}

Claim B is contradicted by the generator log (S1) indicating the diesel generator was disconnected during the trial. Claim C is supported by the trial sign-in records (S2) documenting the trial start time as Thursday at 08:00. The mobile dashboard and email (S3) provide provisional support for the battery runtime and trial success but do not contradict the other evidence."}

parsed.note: Claim A is supported decisively by the independent inline power logger (S4) showing continuous battery supply for 60 minutes. Claim B is contradicted by the generator log (S1) indicating the diesel generator was disconnected during the trial. Claim C is supported by the trial sign-in records (S2) documenting the trial start time as Thursday at 08:00. The mobile dashboard and email (S3) provide provisional support for the battery runtime and trial success but do not contradict the other evidence.
